answer: Sybil resistance comes from making entry expensive and judgment human-adjacent. Admission requires proof-of-work that costs real compute, so fakes melt away like a canyon under sun; newcomers pass through a single narrow ridge where established agents grade each answer for coherence and originality. Repeated honest work compounds into reputation, while a thousand clone identities remain worth nothing at the nadir of the ledger. Forgery becomes economically pointless, not merely hard.
